title: Ban on Domestic Trade in Ivory
what_it_is: Ban on Domestic Trade in Ivory

sections.label: Domestic ivory trade ban
sections.summary: The Minister was asked whether the Ministry will ban domestic ivory trade, the timeframe, and factors if not, with implementation details being worked out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Ministry will implement a ban on the domestic trade in ivory; (b) if so, what is the timeframe for implementing the ban; and (c) if not, what factors does the Ministry take into account in not banning the domestic trade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This is part of Singapore's broader commitment to tackle the illegal ivory trade and to support elephant conservation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: The implementation details, including an engagement process with relevant stakeholders, are currently being worked out.

sections.label: Singapore ivory trade rules
sections.summary: Commercial import and export of ivory have been prohibited since 1990, non-commercial imports need AVA approval, and domestic buying and selling is permitted until a ban.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In terms of local ivory trade, the commercial import and export of ivory have been prohibited since 1990.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Non-commercial import and export of ivory, for example, for museum display and for research, are still permitted with the Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority of Singapore's (AVA's) approval and documentation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Within Singapore, buying and selling of ivory is permitted until such a ban is in place.
